title: DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B / 33B
name: DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B / 33B
description: DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B / 33B is the code-specialized branch of the DeepSeek family and is the variant to choose when code completion, infill, repository-aware generation, and code-adjacent reasoning need to be productionized rather than treated as a general chat problem.

hardware.recommended_gpu: For the 33B variant, community guidance strongly favors high-memory GPUs or multi-GPU serving; for 6.7B, a smaller single-GPU footprint is workable with quantization.

deployment.recommended_quantization: BF16 for the 33B model when fidelity is the priority; use lower-bit quantization for 6.7B when latency and cost matter more than maximum code quality.

license_info.name: MIT License for code; Model License applies to weights
license_info.notes: The official paper and model card both state permissive usage, including commercial use, for DeepSeek-Coder models.

best_for: Code completion and code infill in developer tools.
Repository-aware generation where 16K context is enough for local file neighborhoods.
Code-heavy workflows that need better quality than general-purpose chat models at the same size class.
avoid_for: Non-code workloads where a general chat model would be more cost-efficient.
Very long repository contexts that exceed the model’s reliable 16K operating range.
Small deployment targets that cannot absorb the 33B memory footprint without heavy quantization or multi-GPU partitioning.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Use the 6.7B variant for cost-sensitive code assistants and the 33B variant when code quality justifies a much larger inference footprint.
deployment_risks: Memory sharding issues and latency overhead when partitioning the 33B variant on multi-GPU hardware.
Incorrect infill parser behavior in downstream IDE extensions if the token formatting template is custom-coded incorrectly.
failure_modes: OOM failures under concurrent long-context queries for the 33B variant.
Broken Fill-In-the-Middle formatting parser causing text generation loop.
common_mistakes: Treating 33B as a drop-in replacement for 6.7B without resizing the deployment footprint usually causes memory pressure and throughput collapse.
Running inference in native FP16/BF16 on low-memory servers without using a quantized format for 6.7B.
operational_notes: The model was trained with Fill-In-the-Middle and next-token prediction, so serving should preserve infill-aware prompting and not collapse the model into plain left-to-right completion only.
The 33B model uses grouped-query attention with group size 8, which is the main architectural difference that matters for serving efficiency and memory behavior relative to the 6.7B variant.

The paper recommends FIM-aware prompting and notes that CoT-style prompting can improve difficult coding tasks, especially for instruction-tuned variants, so prompt policy has material quality impact.

The official model card shows standard Hugging Face loading with trust_remote_code=True, so production integration should assume custom model code rather than a generic, architecture-agnostic loader path.

Variant differentiation (Identity): DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B / 33B is the code-specialized branch of the DeepSeek family and is the variant to choose when code completion, infill, repository-aware generation, and code-adjacent reasoning need to be productionized rather than treated as a general chat problem.
Variant differentiation (File Formats): Safetensors format is officially published, while GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ and Apple Silicon MLX/ONNX formats are Not Published in official checkpoints.
Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): 6.7B is comfortable on single-GPU in 4-bit/8-bit forms, while 33B requires multi-GPU layouts or high-memory nodes.
Variant differentiation (Downloads): official checkpoints include Hugging Face base checkpoints, the main GitHub repository, and the technical paper.
Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): vLLM recipes index DeepSeek-Coder families directly, while edge llama.cpp support has no official compatibility statement.
Variant differentiation (Deployment): 33B uses Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) for memory savings, whereas 6.7B relies on standard attention.
Variant differentiation (License): MIT License applies to the code repository, while weights are subject to the model card license terms.
